hints.content: A Winchester rifle bullet travels at a speed of $1{,}924$ miles per hour.  So any equation with a speed *greater* than $1{,}924\,\text{mph}$ will work.  What speeds are represented by the various answer choices?

First, let’s consider $d=1{,}294t$.  If $t=\red1$ hour, then $d=(1{,}294)(\red1)$ miles, so the speed is $1{,}294\,\,\text{mph}$.   Since $1{,}294$ is *less* than $1{,}924$,  this choice does not work.
Which of the remaining answer choices represents a speed greater than $1{,}924$?

The only choices that have a speed greater than $1{,}924\,\,\text{mph}$ are $d=1{,}950t$ and $d=2{,}000t$:

$d=1{,}950t$ has a speed of $1{,}950\,\text{mph}$, and

$d=2{,}000t$ has a speed of $2{,}000\,\text{mph}$.
**$d=1{,}950t$ and $d=2{,}000t$ represent speeds *greater* than a speeding bullet.**

question.content:
Superman was said to be "faster than a speeding bullet."  A Winchester rifle bullet travels at a speed of $1{,}924$ miles per hour $(\text{mph})$. 

**Which of the equations, where $t$ is the time in hours and $d$ the distance in miles,  describe a speed *faster*  than the speed of a Winchester bullet?**
